rationale: Matthew 18:16 (BSB) prints "every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses" inside quotation marks, and the BSB's own footnote on Bible Hub points to Deuteronomy 19:15, which ends "A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses" (BSB). The Greek core matches the Septuagint closely: Swete's text of Deuteronomy 19:15 reads ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων καὶ ἐπὶ στόματος τριῶν μαρτύρων στήσεται πᾶν ῥῆμα, and every edition Bible Hub lists for Matthew 18:16 reads ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων ἢ τριῶν σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα, shortened, with ἢ in place of the repeated phrase and a different form of the verb. Calvin says Christ is "Alluding to that law"; Poole applies to church matters what was "the law of God in civil and judicial causes, Deu 19:15"; the NABRE note reads "Cf. Dt 19:15." No citation formula introduces the words, so the type is allusion rather than quotation, following conn-matt10-household-micah7 (Matthew reusing Old Testament wording without a formula); the close Greek wording and the translators' quotation marks are why the label is strong. The same rule is repeated at Deuteronomy 17:6, 2 Corinthians 13:1, 1 Timothy 5:19 and Hebrews 10:28 (a BSB script search for "two or three witnesses"); those are not part of this row.
